Key Takeaways

A fund that manages $35.8 billion made its three biggest second-quarter adds to MercadoLibre, Danaher and S&P Global.

Danaher and S&P Global are up 23% and 18% since June 30, and MercadoLibre is up 3%.

MercadoLibre has 31% upside to analysts' average target, but its operating margin slipped to 6.3% in the third quarter.

Danaher looks like the best buy of the three, as the only one with a higher average analyst target than a year ago.

Eagle Capital Management, a fund that manages $35.8 billion, made its three biggest adds of the second quarter to MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ), Danaher (DHR:NYSE) and S&P Global (SPGI:NYSE), according to its 13F for the quarter ended June 30, filed Aug. 14.

That filing is still its latest. Since June, two of the three have climbed hard, and over the past year analysts have raised their average target on just one of them.

MercadoLibre is the biggest bet of the three

The fund raised its MercadoLibre stake 79% in the second quarter, to 1.41 million shares worth $2.39 billion at June 30. That's 7.3% of its 13F stocks and its No. 3 position, and the stock is up 3% since.

MercadoLibre reported its third quarter on Nov. 4, and it was more of the same. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion. But operating income fell 6% to $676 million, and the operating margin slipped to 6.3%, from 6.7% in the second quarter and 9.8% a year earlier. The company said the drop came from more free shipping, new fulfillment capacity ahead of its peak season and "a tactical decision to increase affiliate marketing spend in Brazil."

The bulls were counting on profit growth, and they didn't get it. Analysts have been lowering their sights all year, too. Their consensus target is down 21% over the past year, to $2,272 from $2,877:

Shares of MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI have plunged 11.9% since the company reported third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4, reflecting investor concerns over profitability despite robust revenue growth and continued expansion across its commerce and fintech businesses. The sell-off highlights concerns about the company's aggressive investments in logistics, customer acquisition and financial services, which are supporting engagement but weighing on near-term margins.

Over the past three months, MELI shares have lost 16%, underperforming the industry, the Zacks Retail – Wholesale sector and the S&P 500's decline of 8.7%, 3.1% and 5.7%, respectively. The stock has also lagged Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN, which has dipped 3.6% over the same period. However, MELI has performed better than Sea Limited SE, which has tumbled 31.2%.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

With the stock experiencing significant selling pressure, investors face a key question: Does the recent correction present an attractive entry opportunity, or do persistent margin headwinds warrant caution?

MELI's Q3 Results: What Triggered the Sell-Off?

MercadoLibre reported strong third-quarter 2026 revenue growth, but profitability pressures overshadowed its top-line performance. Net revenues and financial income rose 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, reflecting sustained commerce and fintech momentum. However, income from operations declined 6% to $676 million, while operating margin contracted to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier and 6.7% in the preceding quarter.

Net income increased 6% to $448 million, although net margin narrowed to 4.2% from 5.7% year over year. Earnings per share of $8.83 missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.41, adding to investor concerns.

Margin compression primarily reflected higher shipping costs, fulfillment investments and marketing expenses. Net shipping costs created a 60-basis-point sequential margin headwind as lower free-shipping thresholds encouraged smaller, more frequent purchases. Fulfillment capacity expanded nearly 20% sequentially ahead of peak demand, while elevated energy prices increased transportation expenses.

Meanwhile, increased affiliate marketing investments in Brazil pushed sales and marketing expenses up 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of revenues. Higher provisions associated with credit portfolio growth also added to year-over-year profitability pressures.

Although these investments aim to strengthen customer engagement and long-term growth, their near-term earnings impact and uncertainty surrounding margin recovery appear to have contributed to the stock's decline.

Q3 results put MercadoLibre's earnings mix in focus

MercadoLibre (MELI) just posted fresh third quarter numbers that give you plenty to chew on. Revenue for the period reached US$10.75b, while net income came in at US$448m.

Across the first nine months of 2026, the business reported US$29.76b in sales and US$1.33b in profit. Earnings per share for the quarter were US$8.83 on both a basic and diluted basis.

MercadoLibre's share price has fallen 21% over the past three months and is down 22.34% year to date, even though the 3 year total shareholder return is still positive at 11.2%. This points to fading short term momentum after a stronger earlier run.

Spot opportunities other investors might be missing by scanning our 19 high quality undiscovered gems, featuring fundamentals that are similar to what you are monitoring in MercadoLibre today.

The recent slide in MercadoLibre, despite solid headline revenue and mixed profit trends, puts you at a crossroads. Is this reset already generous enough, or does patience for an even cheaper entry make more sense before running the numbers?

Most Popular Narrative: 36% Undervalued

On the numbers provided, the most followed narrative pegs MercadoLibre's fair value at about $2,395 per share, compared with a last close of $1,532. That gap is what turns the focus onto how much of today's rapid expansion will eventually turn into cash that shareholders actually keep.

According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the entire debate starts with how you treat MercadoLibre's lending build out and the cash it soaks up.

Under my modeled revenue path, a $1,530 share price can be reproduced if MercadoLibre's owner-cash-flow margin improves from an illustrative starting level near 3.2% to approximately 5.1% over the next decade.

My central case assumes 8.5%.

See why 158 investors see MercadoLibre as 36% undervalued.

Using the narrative's own ten year framework and 11.45% discount rate, the fair value of $2,395 anchors on revenue and financial income progressing from around $40b, while owner cash flow gradually steps up toward that 8.5% margin assumption. The reference price near $1,530 is then essentially the market "pricing in" a milder improvement in cash conversion, closer to the 5.1% margin that backs out of the model when all other inputs stay the same.

That is why the same MercadoLibre financials can support very different conclusions. If operating profitability and owner cash generation trend toward the higher margin path outlined by John_Eric, the narrative argues the current share price undervalues that outcome. If margins stall closer to the lower band, the apparent discount in the headline 36% gap could shrink quickly.

Yet CFO Martín de los Santos reminded us of the company's strength. He said, "Users are buying more often and entrusting more of their money to Mercado Pago." Indeed, revenue grew 45%, despite disappointing earnings. I think that split explains the opportunity. Today's growth investment could produce much stronger earnings, while the decline has made MELI's valuation considerably more appealing, making me bullish on the stock.

MercadoLibre's Q3 Growth Remains Exceptional

MercadoLibre's Q3 growth was exceptional, in my opinion, despite the earnings miss. The report showed revenue and financial income rising 45% to $10.75 billion. MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) sank 9% on a profit miss last week. Days later, the latest episode of the We Study Billionaires podcast came out under the title "We Doubled Down on Meli."

Growth wasn't the issue. Third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, while the operating margin fell to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier.

Shawn O'Malley was defending the growth forecasts in Daniel Mahncke's model on the episode when he reminded listeners that "Meli is the only company ever at significant size that was able to grow 30% or more for 30 consecutive quarters straight."

Then MercadoLibre added a logistics bill in the third quarter. CFO Martin de los Santos said on the call that the company grew its logistics capacity 20% from the second quarter ahead of the holiday peak, against 10% a year earlier. He expects part of that cost to come back in the fourth quarter.

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is prioritizing customer engagement and marketplace expansion even as these investments weigh on margins. In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10,750 million, yet operating income slipped 6% to $676 million. Operating margin declined 40 basis points sequentially to 6.3%, reflecting the cost of more free shipping, expanded fulfillment capacity ahead of peak season and increased affiliate marketing spending in Brazil.

Management identified a 60-basis-point sequential margin headwind from net shipping costs, including expenses associated with network expansion. Lower free-shipping thresholds encouraged customers to place smaller, more frequent orders, reducing revenue per shipment even as volumes increased. Higher energy prices added transportation costs, while fulfillment square footage expanded nearly 20% quarter over quarter ahead of peak demand. The expansion also brought temporary recruitment expenses. Meanwhile, sales and marketing spending rose 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of revenues as MercadoLibre stepped up affiliate investment in Brazil.

Despite these cost pressures, MercadoLibre reported measurable improvements in logistics efficiency. In Brazil, items sold increased 45% year over year, while cost per shipment fell 5% year over year in local currency and 14% from the first quarter of 2025 before the lower free-shipping threshold took effect. Management also reported that free & slow shipments in the R$19-R$79 price range in Brazil became variable contribution-positive as a group for the first time in September. Shipments per route reached a new high during the quarter.

These improvements show that MercadoLibre is working to lower delivery costs by handling more orders and improving efficiency. However, the company continues to balance the costs of expanding its shipping network and attracting customers against the efficiency gains from higher shipment volumes.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares tumble 17.2% over the past three months compared with the industry's 8.7% decline. While Amazon shares have fallen 6.7%, Sea Limited has plunged 34% in the aforementioned period.

However, the stock is trading below its 12-month median level of 33.91. MercadoLibre is trading at a premium to Amazon (forward 12-month P/E of 23.43) and Sea Limited (14.97).

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Do Earnings Estimates Signal for MercadoLibre?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year earnings per share has increased by 12 cents to $38.21 over the past seven days. However, the consensus estimate for the next fiscal year has declined by 10 cents to $55.09 during the same period.

The consensus estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year sales indicates year-over-year growth of 45.1%, while the consensus estimate for earnings per share suggests a 3% decline. For the next fiscal year, the consensus estimates project sales and earnings growth of 28.9% and 44.2%, respectively.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

MELI's Investment Case

MercadoLibre's strong marketplace growth, rising customer engagement and expanding fintech ecosystem support its long-term prospects. Improving logistics efficiency and increasing purchase frequency strengthen its competitive positioning. However, elevated shipping costs, continued investments and margin pressure constrain near-term profitability. Its premium valuation also warrants caution despite encouraging revenue growth and improving operational efficiencies. MELI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 4, 2026, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) announced an FX-neutral revenue increase of 41% year over year alongside $676 million in operating income. Management sacrificed 40 basis points of operating margin to fund logistics capacity and affiliate marketing. Long-term investors need to know if these upfront spending choices build lasting competitive advantages. Three key takeaways from management explain how these capital choices position the business.

1. Logistics Expansion Sacrifices Short-Term Margin for Scale

MercadoLibre expanded its fulfillment footprint by nearly 20% in the third quarter ahead of the peak shopping season, incurring upfront costs before shipping volume arrived. Despite these short-term shipping headwinds, shipping cost per unit in Brazil dropped 5% year over year on an FX-neutral basis.

We added almost 20% to our fulfillment square meters quarter-on-quarter ahead of peak. That cost lands before the volume does, a pattern we have seen many times since we started operating fulfillment almost 10 years ago.
-- Martin de los Santos, Chief Financial Officer

2. Affiliate Marketing Investments Drive Social Commerce Acceleration

Management allocated extra capital to its social media creator network in Brazil, pushing sales and marketing expenses up 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of net revenue. The regional affiliate network surpassed 12 million members, expanding product discovery beyond traditional search channels.

Orders through the channel grew 240% year-on-year. Consumers increasingly discover and buy products through creators and social media.
-- Martin de los Santos, Chief Financial Officer

3. E-Commerce Customer Data Protects Credit Portfolio Performance

MercadoLibre expanded its credit portfolio 62% year over year while maintaining non-performing loans, or NPLs, aged 15 to 90 days at 7%. First-party shopping data from the marketplace allows the company to evaluate buyer risk before issuing credit lines.

And coming back to Brazil, I would say that an important advantage is that the marketplace gives us information before we lend. And we see how users buy, how they pay, how they use installments.
-- Osvaldo Gimenez, President of Fintech

Looking Ahead

Executive focus remains centered on artificial intelligence integration and proprietary ecosystem features. Internal development efforts prioritize in-house software capabilities over external platform integrations to safeguard customer relationships.

MercadoLibre's most recent quarter was met with a negative market reaction, as investors focused on profitability pressures despite strong topline growth. Management attributed the margin compression to deliberate investments in logistics and sales and marketing, particularly in Brazil, where the company expanded fulfillment capacity and ramped up its social commerce affiliate program. CFO Martín de los Santos explained that these decisions, including lowering the free shipping threshold and adding fulfillment space ahead of peak season, were intended to drive deeper customer engagement and future revenue growth, even though they weighed on operating margins in the short term.

MercadoLibre (MELI) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $10.75 billion vs S&P analysts' estimates of $10.64 billion (45.1% year-on-year growth, 1% beat)

Adjusted EPS $8.83 vs S&P analysts' expectations of $9.18 (3.8% miss)

Adjusted EBITDA $982 million vs analyst estimates of $984.7 million (9.1% margin, in line)

Operating margin 6.3%, down from 9.8% in the same quarter last year

Unique active buyers 108.8 million, up 31.8 million year on year

Market capitalization $77.58 billion

While we enjoy listening to the management's commentary, our favorite part of earnings calls is the analyst questions. Those are unscripted and can often highlight topics that management teams would rather avoid or topics where the answer is complicated. Here is what has caught our attention.

Our top 5 analyst questions from MercadoLibre's Q3 earnings call

Andrew Ruben (Morgan Stanley) asked about the long-term significance of social commerce and affiliate marketing. CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn emphasized that affiliates are now a strategic investment and core to MercadoLibre's approach as consumer shopping habits shift toward social platforms.

Irma Sgarz (Goldman Sachs) questioned whether there are new, significant investment priorities on the horizon. CFO Martín de los Santos stated that major initiatives remain consistent, with shipping and affiliate marketing as the main levers, and no major new spending areas planned in the near term.

Marcelo Santos (JPMorgan) probed the outlook for credit quality amid macro headwinds in Brazil. President of Fintech Osvaldo Giménez highlighted disciplined risk management, noting stable non-performing loan ratios and a cautious approach in more vulnerable lending segments.

Josh Beck (Raymond James) inquired about the financial impact and future of AI investments, as well as the potential of agentic shopping. De los Santos confirmed current AI investments are generating positive returns, and Szarfsztejn explained that agentic shopping will be developed in-house rather than opening the platform to third parties.

Neha Agarwala (HSBC) asked about payment take rates and margin trends. Giménez and Szarfsztejn pointed to device cost fluctuations and mix shifts as drivers but expressed confidence in long-term profitability and margin stability across payment and merchant lending businesses.

title: MercadoLibre's Profits Fall Again. What It Means for Investors

Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool

MELI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) delivered another round of strong top-line growth, but falling profits again sank the stock.

Shares fell 12% on Thursday as investors have grown impatient with the company's investment cycle, as it spends on lower free shipping thresholds, expanded logistics, and growing its credit business. However, that again led to narrower margins.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Revenue in the quarter jumped 45% to $10.75 billion, edging out estimates of $10.71 billion. Both core businesses delivered strong growth, with gross merchandise volume up 38% to $23 billion, and total payment volume jumped 53% to $109 billion.

Operating income in the quarter fell from $636 million to $601 million, and the company reported a net income margin of just 4.2%. On a per-share basis, earnings rose from $8.32 to $8.83 as the company benefited from lower tax expense. Still, that was below analyst estimates at $9.27.

MercadoLibre doesn't give guidance, so estimates are a bit of a guessing game, which works against the stock at times like these when it's investing in the business.

Image source: Getty Images.

Are its investments paying off?

The top-line metrics are clearly moving in the right direction, and management said it gained share in its three largest markets, Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina, which should quell concerns about competition from Amazon and Sea Limited's Shopee.

Importantly, the company continued to see engagement strengthening, and it sees a significant opportunity to grow purchase frequency, noting that its buyers make an average of 12 purchases a year, compared to more than 50 for e-commerce shoppers in developed countries. Faster shipping, lowering the free shipping threshold, and expanding its selection are part of its strategy to build a sticky habit and strengthen its competitive advantage, much like Amazon has done in the U.S.

The company is also seeing more customers adopt multiple products, which drive both revenue and margin improvement over the long run. As the business has scaled up, its cost per shipment in Brazil has fallen, down 5% in constant currency over the last year and 14% since the first quarter of 2025, a sign that it's effectively scaling its logistics operations.

Its credit card portfolio has been another source of headwinds on the bottom line, as the company needs to book a provision for expected losses when it issues new cards, even before it's earned any profits. The credit portfolio grew 62% to $18 billion in the quarter, and default and interest metrics remained stable.

Key Points

Interested in MercadoLibre, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Mercado Libre's Q3 revenue grew 45.1% year over year to $10.75 billion, but aggressive investment spending caused operating margin to decline to 6.3% from 9.8%.

Shares have fallen toward key technical support near $1,540 after Brazil's election sell-off, though analysts maintain bullish ratings with price targets implying roughly 45% upside.

The company's long-term outlook depends on whether elevated spending on shipping, fintech, and marketing eventually eases, allowing margins to widen amid rising competition from Amazon and Temu.

Mercado Libre's (NASDAQ: MELI) stock price has been under pressure since mid-2025 when it announced a more aggressive investment cycle.

Choosing market share and volume over near-term profits, the company is expanding an integrated e-commerce and fintech ecosystem across Latin America.

→ Could the Midterms Revive Medicare for All? 3 Healthcare Stocks to Watch

The net result is sustained, high-level growth and impressive earnings per share, just not quite as impressive as the earnings would be if not for the investments.

Mercado Libre's Q3 earnings report reinforced that trade-off, with strong revenue growth overshadowed by shrinking margins. With shares testing key technical support, investors face a familiar question: Is the weakness creating a buying opportunity, or is the stock's recovery still dependent on improving profitability?

→ Qualcomm Beat Earnings, But Its Fastest-Growing Businesses Have a Catch

Mercado Libre Stock Tests Key Support as Analysts Weigh the Upside

A combination of downward analyst price revisions and political uncertainty has weighed on Mercado Libre shares, leaving the stock susceptible to further sell-offs.

Brazil's political environment, especially the presidential runoff on Oct. 25, added another source of pressure. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's unexpected reelection triggered a broad sell-off in Brazilian assets, including Mercado Libre shares, and heightened concerns about currency volatility. The sell-off pushed MELI toward its recent lows, raising the possibility that the stock is establishing a bottom.

→ Google's Credit Backstop May Be TeraWulf's Biggest Advantage

At least one analyst called out MELI's post-election plunge as an overreaction: BTIG's Marvin Fong also pointed to foreign exchange (FX) conversion as the near-term risk and said investors should look to the Q3 and Q4 results for clarity. Morgan Stanley's Andrew Rubin echoed the sentiment, highlighting FX risk alongside the company's strengths.

Among those strengths is its expanding credit portfolio, which is not tied to local rates.

Rubin also views a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 27 times projected 2027 earnings as an attractive entry point. That would put the stock in the $ 1,500 to $ 1,600 range, depending on the estimate—lower than the early-November price action, but aligned with a technical bottom. The technical support is approximately $1,540 and has been tested through by two successive rebounds, including one triggered by the election sell-off.

Analysts' price targets remain attractive, with the lowest target at $1,750 and the consensus target near $2,200, reflecting about 45% upside.

Recent revisions, however, have been mixed. Following Q3 earnings, BTIG lowered its price target to $2,050, while Cantor Fitzgerald reduced its target to $2,000. Both firms maintained bullish ratings, suggesting continued confidence in Mercado Libre's longer-term prospects despite near-term profitability concerns.

The question is what might put analysts in a more bullish posture. Signs of strength would likely alleviate fear of near-term margin compression and improve long-term visibility.

Institutional data suggests this group will limit downside risk as the year progresses. Institutions own approximately 88% of the stock, a sign of strong conviction, and have accumulated on balance this year.

The red flag is that early Q4 activity has been relatively balanced, reflecting uncertainty ahead of the Q3 earnings release on Nov. 4, and could easily tip into distribution if the company's outlook deteriorates.

MELI falls to key support level after Q3 results.
Mercado Libre's Q3 Earnings Reveal the Cost of Aggressive Growth

Mercado Libre'sQ3 results failed to trigger an immediately bullish stock price response, but that doesn't make them any less impressive in terms of growth.

The problem is profitability. Net margin came in at 4.2%, while operating margin declined to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier, reflecting the costs of aggressive investments in shipping, fulfillment, and marketing. Revenue grew 45.1% year over year (YOY) to $10.75 billion, driven by strength in both operating segments and outpacing MarketBeat's reported consensus.

On the retail side, total payment value grew 53% YOY to $109 billion, gross merchandise volume grew 38%, and the number of products sold increased 36%. User growth and penetration were also solid, revealing the success of management's strategy. Unique average buyers increased 22%, itmes per buyer increased 12%, and same- and next-day shipping improved 49%, revealing the rapid integration of MELI services into local lifestyles.

On the fintech side, assets under management rose 67%, the credit portfolio grew 62%, and monthly active users grew 29%, fueling strong cash flow and a positive outlook.

Could Mercado Libre's Investment Strategy Unlock Higher Profits?

One risk for investors is the timing and peak of spending. The company has not established a clear timetable for when its aggressive investment cycle will moderate, and elevated spending could continue for years. In this scenario, spending fears and margin compression could keep MELI shares from reaching their full potential.

The opportunity, however, is the transition from aggressive investment to harvesting profits. Eventually, spending could slow, allowing margins to widen and MELI to experience a strong surge in earnings growth, potentially unlocking price-multiple expansion.

Spending headwinds aside, Mercado Libre continues to generate strong earnings per share (EPS). In Q3, the company reported $8.83 in GAAP EPS and $285 million in adjusted free cash flow, helping to sustain balance sheet health and advance its strategy.

The majority of the company's debt is tied to fintech and offset by corresponding receivables and low net leverage. Net debt, including fintech debt, runs at about 2x adjusted EBITDA, a manageable level given the company's financial position. Excluding fintech debt, the company maintains a net cash position. Major credit rating agencies rate it investment grade, though on the low end of the investment-grade spectrum.

Mercado Libre's biggest threat is competition. Now that it's opened the e-commerce gates, companies like Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Temu (NASDAQ: PDD) are moving in. The risk is lost share, sluggish growth, and persistently compressed margins as the company fights to retain leadership.
